warning: This is not PP.4 Core certification evidence. It was produced by hand-swapping a locally built o3kd binary into a retained rc.22 debug VM, which the campaign rules allow only for development confirmation. Final evidence must come from the public successor candidate installed on a fresh host.
purpose: Confirm that the bounded Keystone unscoped-authentication change makes the pinned unmodified Horizon client able to establish an authenticated session, before spending a release candidate on it.

observed_identity_sequence: login POST -> 302 / and an authenticated Horizon session

correction_to_the_accepted_assumption.note: Both routes are the same upstream capability, identity:list_projects_for_user. The witness implements both; only the /v3/users/{user_id}/projects form is exercised by this client. This was found only by capturing the real sequence, which the campaign rules require instead of assuming it.

remaining_proven_mandatory_gaps.why_required: The Horizon instance table resolves each server's project name through api.keystone.tenant_list, which calls keystoneclient projects.list() -> GET /v3/projects. Confirmed by the server-side traceback in openstack_dashboard/dashboards/identity/projects/views.py:107.
remaining_proven_mandatory_gaps.authorization_status: NOT AUTHORIZED by the accepted bounded slice. The campaign brief explicitly withholds general project listing (and all /v3/projects CRUD) unless a real client request proves it mandatory and it receives separate baseline approval. The request is now proven mandatory; the approval is outstanding.

conclusion: The rc.22 login blocker is fixed and the pinned unmodified client now reaches an authenticated session with project context. PP.4 Core is still not certifiable: the required bounded instances panel and native-server visibility do not work yet, and the remaining gaps are outside the authorized slice.
secrets: No credentials recorded; the Horizon session key used is a clearly non-secret local literal.
